evidence.note: Explicit ordered breakdown into subsystems before coding: '1. CLI dev/build/start, 2. Vite plugin shimming next/*...' framing pages-router basics as the first target — identifying major subsystems and a sensible order (plugin/shims → routing → SSR).

Repeatedly reasoned about sequencing: 'build the simplest viable scaffolding that gets pages-basic working with simple navigation' — deliberately established a thin vertical slice (dev server + one pages route) before layering features, dependency-aware (defers app-router/RSC as heaviest).

After first test run (12/325), re-planned ordering by observed coupling: recognized app-router tests don't even RUN without a server, so decided to 'make app-router at least start' so its tests execute, while extracting max value from pages-router first — revisiting sequence as build revealed reality.

Later sequencing degenerates into opportunistic 'quick wins' chasing failure categories (shallow routing, hash routing, ISR, __NEXT_DATA__) rather than a milestone plan with explicit done-criteria; no TodoWrite / written milestone tracking anywhere in 302 steps.

Final state summarizes subsystems shipped (CLI, plugin, pages+app router, SSR/SSG/ISR, middleware, shims) — showing subsystem awareness throughout, but the through-line was reactive test-driven rather than a maintained milestone decomposition with interfaces managed.

reasoning: The agent clearly identified the major subsystems and chose a dependency-aware order — plugin/shims before routing before SSR, deferring app-router/RSC — and notably established a minimal end-to-end pages-router slice under dev before layering features, gating each step on the Playwright suite and re-planning when a first run revealed app-router tests couldn't even execute (steps 13, 50-85). This exceeds anchor 5 (sensible order + rough done-notion). But it falls short of 8: there is no articulated milestone plan with explicit per-milestone done-criteria (no TodoWrite, no written tracking), and after the initial slice the sequencing became opportunistic quick-win chasing driven by failure categories rather than deliberate interface-managed milestone boundaries. That places it solidly between 5 and 8, at a 6.
